curriculum.title: Agriculture- Plant Science Alternate Lesson Plan Template

dimensions.label: Clarity of learning objective
dimensions.note: Student-facing “will be able to” goals appear, but they stay generic (define/explain agriculture and its components) and do not state a clear, purposeful outcome tied to plant science, soil, or career exploration shown elsewhere.

evidence.excerpt: The students will be able to: Define agriculture and explain agriculture industry. Describe the various components of the agriculture industry.

dimensions.label: Engagement / relevance
dimensions.note: The opening Engage uses a timed sticky-note prompt (“How do we grow Plants?”), peer sharing, and posting notes as tree leaves to activate prior knowledge—a clear, interactive hook. The task engages students but the prompt stays generic, without a strong personal or local relevance tie, so it is solid rather than exemplary.

evidence.excerpt: Activate prior knowledge: Pass around a sticky note to each student and place the prompt on slide two of the Agriculture- Plant Science Alternate Lesson Plan Slides

dimensions.label: Checks for understanding
dimensions.note: The lesson includes an explicit Evaluate check—a 3-2-1 Reflection handout—plus related question stems on soil, which is a clear formative close. It is solid but generic: the text does not show criteria, sampling, or how responses will adjust instruction.

evidence.excerpt: Upon completion, have students complete the 3-2-1 Reflection handout over this lesson.

dimensions.label: Differentiation & language supports
dimensions.note: The lesson shows only generic access moves—small-group note-taking and guided notes—without ELPS/language objectives, SpEd/504 accommodations, or GT/extension options. Supports for varied learners are therefore weak and undifferentiated.

evidence.excerpt: Students will take notes and collaborate in small groups. Students will document their understanding through the provided guided notes.

dimensions.label: Cognitive rigor
dimensions.note: The soil lab has students collect, flatten, and closely examine real soil samples before answering property-focused questions, which is clear application beyond recall. The paired stems stay mostly factual (importance/properties/soil vs. dirt), so rigor is solid but not deeply analytical.

evidence.excerpt: the student can have a better look at their soil and answer the questions on their Let’s Find Out About Soil handout.

dimensions.label: Coherent sequence & closure
dimensions.note: E1 shows a timed Evaluate close via a 3-2-1 Reflection, so some end-of-lesson consolidation is present. It remains generic (“over this lesson”) and does not itself evidence a purposeful open-to-practice-to-close arc or specific synthesis of the lesson’s learning.

evidence.excerpt: Upon completion, have students complete the 3-2-1 Reflection handout over this lesson.
